articles.title: Google is making Pixel HiLight slightly more useful
articles.summary: As part of the November 2026 Pixel Drop, the Pixel 11 Pro HiLight light can glow up when you get Google Messages texts from your favorite contacts. Google is also rolling out the Create My Widget feature.
articles.body: Google is adding a new feature to its underwhelming HiLight light on the back of Pixel 11 Pro phones: as part of the November 2026 Pixel Drop, the light can light up when you get Google Messages texts from your favorite contacts. Sure, it’s a small addition to the disappointing ways you could use HiLight at the Pixel 11 Pro’s August launch, which included glowing when you used Gemini and lighting up for calls from your favorite contacts. But it’s something! Fortunately, that’s not everything included in the Pixel Drop, as there are a bunch of other new features coming to a wider range of Pixel devices. The “Create My Widget” feature to build a custom widget with a prompt is rolling out to Pixel 11 and Pixel 10 phones. Google is bringing Gemini Intelligence features to Pixel 10 devices, including the Rambler transcription tool. Users with Pixel 11 and Pixel 10 phones will be able to have Gemini make calls on your behalf to help with tasks like making reservations or checking inventory. If you have a Pixel Watch 3 or newer, you’ll be able to see step-by-step instructions during workouts. And users on Pixel 6A phones and newer will be able to take advantage of a new “Family Hub” spot in settings that consolidates family management controls. Google is also announcing today that its Pixel Tag item tracker is now available. It was originally announced in August.

articles.title: Google’s Pixel Tag tracker is now available
articles.summary: The Pixel Tag is Google’s answer to Apple’s AirTag but is designed to work with Android’s Find Hub app and tracking network.
articles.body: After years of third-party Android trackers from companies like Samsung, Motorola, and Pebblebee, Google’s Pixel Tag is now available for purchase. First announced in August, the Pixel Tag is designed to work with Google’s tracking network and app that was renamed the Find Hub last year. The Pixel Tag is priced similar to Apple’s AirTag 2. A single tracker costs $29.99 while a four-pack is discounted to $99.99. At 0.4 ounces, the Pixel Tag is slightly lighter than the AirTag 2 and while its oblong design is longer than Apple’s tracker, Google’s is a bit thinner. It doesn’t include a hole to attach it to keys, luggage, or other items you want to track, but you can pair it with accessories that make it easy to tether to objects. Unlike Apple’s AirTags, the Pixel Tag has a button that can be pressed to trigger a sound should your phone get misplaced instead of the tracker. [Product: Google Pixel Tag | Google says the Pixel Tag will run for over a year on a single CR2032 coin battery, and it has an IP67 rating so it’s dustproof and can survive a shallow dunking. The tracker also features ultra wideband (UWB) support and Channel Sounding through Bluetooth 6.0. Android phones with a UWB chip can display the exact distance and direction to the Pixel Tag in the Find Hub app once you’re close to it, while Bluetooth Channel Sounding is limited to just distance. The Pixel Tag is compatible with smartphones running Android 9 or later, but you’ll need devices that specifically include a UWB chip or support Bluetooth 6.0 to take advantage of Find Hub’s precise locating features.

articles.title: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”
articles.body:
Oura announced on Tuesday that it’s acquiring AI-native primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”

Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Its service was integrated into the Oura app in June.

Users can connect with Counsel’s medical AI to get personalized medical advice, and chat with a physician when needed, all within the Oura app. Now, the companies plan to expand on their existing partnership to build across preventative care, acute care, and specialty and chronic care.

While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By acquiring Counsel Health, Oura is looking to expand its business and help users access medical care.

“Oura helps members understand their physiology and, with Counsel, they can take action on their health across a range of needs, from quick questions and prescriptions to lab results, chronic care, and referrals,” said Oura CEO Tom Hale in a press release .

Counsel Health raised a $25 million Series A a year ago, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and GV. PitchBook estimates it had raised a total of $36 million.

Following the acquisition, Oura says Counsel will continue serving existing and new enterprise partners, with the goal of expanding its AI-native care model to more people beyond Oura’s membership.

Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, alongside the company’s 70 employees, Bloomberg reports.

“At Counsel, we’ve built medical AI around trust, safety and responsibility, keeping physicians in the loop for clinical decisions,” Alagappan said in the press release. “Oura’s data gives clinicians objective context, trended biometrics, and member engagement to deliver more informed care. From the start, our teams bonded over a joint vision, shared culture, and mission, further solidifying as we negotiated our deal over the past few months.”

The deal is expected to close before the end of 2027.

Oura also announced that its revenue grew 153% year-over-year to $533 million for the quarter ended on September 30. For its fiscal year 2026, Oura generated revenue of approximately $1.75 billion, marking 92% year-over-year growth.

The company reached an $11 billion valuation following a $900 million late-stage funding round in October 2025.

articles.title: Oura is acquiring medical AI chatbot startup Counsel Health
articles.summary: Smart ring maker Oura announced a $625 million deal to buy medical AI startup Counsel Health.
articles.body: Oura announced its quarterly earnings today and said it agreed to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, after adding the company’s AI chatbot to its app earlier this year. Counsel Health calls itself an “AI-native primary care company,” using the app to deliver AI-generated responses and insights based on users’ health data reported from their wearables that can then proceed to a conversation with one of its in-house physicians. Oura says it expects the deal to close before the end of the year. Oura CEO Tom Hale said in an interview with Bloomberg that the acquisition is part of a plan to connect wearables, clinical AI, and access to doctors based on insights from biometric data to answer questions or monitor ongoing conditions. Counsel Health’s AI chatbot can connect Oura users to a real doctor directly from the app and draw on users’ biometric data from their wearables in its answers to medical questions. The plan they describe in the press release is to focus on three areas, including preventative care, acute care for episodic health concerns, and specialty and chronic care for things like reproductive and cardiometabolic health. According to Bloomberg, Counsel Health’s CEO Muthu Alagappan says it’s also planning to expand its network of on-demand physicians, which is currently “made up of about 50 people.” Counsel’s 70 employees will join Oura as part of the deal, with Alagappan becoming Oura’s chief clinical AI officer. Oura says in its announcement that Counsel will also continue offering its medical AI platform outside of Oura’s user base through new and existing enterprise partners, including “health plans, health systems, consumer health organizations, and employers.”

articles.title: The VR Disney Plus app on Meta Quest now has 3D movies
articles.summary: Disney is bringing more than 60 3D movies to the Disney Plus app on Meta Quest. The movies will be available to Disney Plus subscribers as part of an updated Disney Plus app that’s rolling out today.
articles.body: Disney is bringing more than 60 3D movies to the Disney Plus app on Meta Quest. The movies will be available to Disney Plus subscribers as part of an updated Disney Plus app that’s rolling out today. The 3D movies you can check out include The Avengers and Black Panther, Meta says. But the updated Quest app doesn’t just offer 3D movies; you’ll also be able to see some films in themed, immersive virtual environments, like a Tatooine environment when watching Star Wars: A New Hope or a Scare Floor one for Monsters, Inc. I got to see an Avengers-themed immersive environment for myself while trying Meta’s forthcoming VR Glasses in September, and while it was novel for the few minutes I tried it, I wasn’t sure if it would be good during an entire movie. The Disney Plus app on the VR Glasses, which are set to release sometime in spring 2027, will also let you watch IMAX Enhanced movies, including Avengers: Endgame, Lightyear, and Tron: Ares. The VR Glasses will also be a place to watch 3D movies from Lionsgate.

articles.title: “Dancing With the Stars ”Grammy Night recap: Music icon cameos and an absolute shocker elimination
articles.summary: Salsas and tangos to hits by Janet Jackson and Beyoncé made for a splashy evening that saw the final seven narrowed down to six.
articles.body:
The final seven couples on Dancing With the Stars season 35 duked it out to award-winning hits on week 9 of the competition — Grammy Night.

After the elimination of actress Julia Stiles and her pro partner, Ezra Sosa, the remaining celebs who rank low, like Maura Higgins and Tatyana Ali, danced hard to save their spots.

Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy earned praise for their jazz routine, got a special video message from Janet Jackson, and won their dance-off, but were still sent packing.

I'd like to thank the Academy — for the tickets to this hit parade on Dancing With the Stars !

Welcome to Grammy Night on DWTS season 35. It is already the ninth week of the competition, though it seems like it was just yesterday that this season's 16 celebs and their pro partners descended on the ballroom, with glory on the horizon and hope in their hearts. There have been a whopping nine eliminations since then, and the one many fans feared the most happened on last week's Disney Night .

Julia Stiles, the iconic star of '90s classics like Save the Last Dance and 10 Things I Hate About You , was sent packing alongside her pro partner, Ezra Sosa. At least they have matching tattoos to commiserate! With only seven couples left standing, there's very little fat left to trim. It was less certain than ever who would be following Stiles and Sosa when cohosts Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough read out that dreaded name.

This week, the remaining pairs were tasked with choreographing and drilling down routines to Grammy-winning hits, from Janet Jackson's "All For You" to Evanescence's "Bring Me to Life." Though judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough, and Bruno Tonioli are totally aligned in their love of some couples (actress Jenna Dewan and pro Val Chmerkovskiy have previously gotten two consecutive perfect scores), they've also clashed over others whose dance game is still growing. Example: Inaba holding up the sole 9 paddle for actress Tatyana Ali and pro Jan Ravnik last week.

Week 9 was destined to be a crowded one. The evening was set to feature live performances from Brandy, Monica, Maren Morris, and Sheryl Crow, for starters. And as the time needed to showcase each dance decreases with each elimination, production makes up for it by programming special dance-offs at the tail-end of episodes.

Grammy Night had a planned finale of several couples competing against each other by dancing to the same song. The face-offs included Dewan and Chmerkovskiy vs. Ali and Ravnik, podcaster Connor Wood and pro Rylee Arnold vs. reality star Maura Higgins and pro Mark Ballas, and Paralympian Ezra Frech and pro Daniella Karagach vs. Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn and pro Pasha Pashkov.

Frech and Karagach kicked off the night with a fiery Argentine tango to a remix of Beyoncé's "Crazy in Love." "This song is a very intimate dance. It's passionate; it does not give brother and sister energy," Frech joked, which Inaba picked up on after they slayed the choreography in the ballroom. Calling it the "hardest dance you've done so far," Inaba praised Frech for staying "so centered on yourself," and for "turning your sister into your lover for one night." Okay!

Next up was Frech's Olympic comrade Glenn, who expressed in rehearsals that she was determined to make up for a misstep that Inaba caught in their quickstep last week. She "channeled that teen angst I had" that she "couldn't express because I was a figure skater" into a tortured paso doble to Evanescence's "Bring Me to Life," which scored a high 28. Noting Sexiest DWTS Dancer Pashkov's shirtlessness, Derek joked, "That paso had power, it had precision, it had purpose, it had Pasha!"

Next up was Higgins, whom Inaba threw a similar gauntlet when she noted last week that, during her jive with Ballas, "at times the energy dropped." She was set on sending the energy through the roof, and then suffered a rib injury serious enough that it required an X-ray. "You are a warrior for doing that dance with that injury," Inaba raved. "That was, for me, a work of art." And so was Dewan's jazz routine to Janet Jackson's "All For You," which she danced every night on stage with Jackson 24 years ago when she joined the All For You Tour as a backup dancer.

After scoring two perfect 40s on back-to-back weeks, Dewan and Chmerkovskiy knocked it out of the park again, tying Glenn and Pashkov at the top with a 28. Then Julianne intro'd a video message from Jackson direct to Dewan, who told her old tour buddy that she was "so excited. I cannot wait to watch you perform tonight, and you're performing to 'All For You!' I feel so honored... I know you're going to do an incredible job. Weren't those such fun times back in those days?"

Ali and Ravnik then hit the ballroom with a Tango to "Boom Boom Pow" by The Black Eyed Peas. Mrs. Hollywood herself casually dropped the lore that she befriended Black Eyed Peas frontman Will.i.am while at Harvard, and has stayed close to the musician ever since. So this dance was personal — and performed live for Will.i.am, who joined the crowd in the ballroom! Derek praised Ali's "way of drawing us in," while Tonioli called her a "Tarantino leading lady."

Ali and Ravnik may have earned their highest score ever with three 9s ("I feel so overwhelmed, I don't have the right words!" she cried), but Wood was still reeling from getting all 8s last week. Still, he noted, he was able to lead his team to victory in the team dance-off, but would he make an impression on Grammy Night? His and Arnold's Argentine tango to "SexyBack" by Justin Timberlake scored a mere 27, so not really. But Wood still celebrated, "This has been the fastest development as a person I think I've ever had!"

Last up was Shum, who has been crushing the competition with two-time Mirrorball winner Johnson. During rehearsals, Shum detailed how being born in Costa Rica meant that he grew up watching "people dancing salsa, always as an observer... I'm excited to tap into my roots." As per usual, tap in he did, earning a near-perfect score and leaving Inaba exclaiming, "That made my smile, because you've got the style, you've got the showmanship... Dance is life, and you had the moment."

Then it was time for the dance-offs. Glenn and Frech were first up, and their rumba to "The Boy Is Mine" by Brandy & Monica (singing live!) was praised by Derek as "one of the most satisfying dance-offs I think we've ever seen." Glenn and Pashkov won, adding two points to their score. Dewan and Chmerkovskiy followed suit by winning their dance-off with Ali and Ravnik to "The Middle" by Maren Morris (another live performance!), and Higgins and Ballas won their showdown to "All I Wanna Do" by Sheryl Crow (live yet again, millennials everywhere are screaming!) against Wood and Arnold.

When all was said and done, Ribeiro and Julianne narrowed the final seven down to just two: Ali and Ravnik, and, when it seemed like it was about to be the other couple straggling at the back of the pack, Wood and Arnold, Ribeiro marked them safe. That left Dewan and Chmerkovskiy, who were hot off a back-to-back run of exceptionally strong dances, in the bottom two.

It seemed like there was no way Ali would survive that final call, but #TatyanaNation rose up and delivered for their star. Dewan and Chmerkovskiy's names were read as the week's eliminees.

"This is shocking to say the least, but what would you like to say?" a stunned Julianne asked Dewan, who was all grace. "Dancing again, getting to share my joy with my family, who is over here, every single night. I had a great time. I loved getting to share that with the world, honestly, all love." After Dewan said her final piece, Shum, her fellow former backup dancer and ABC star (Dewan appears on The Rookie , while Shum appears on Grey's Anatomy ), gave her the first in a series of long, sympathetic hugs.

New episodes of Dancing With the Stars season 35 air on Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET/PT on ABC and Disney+.
